props.title: March or Die

sections.content: March or Die (1977) represents a fascinating entry in the Foreign Legion subgenre of war films, starring Gene Hackman as Major Foster, a hardened Legion commander leading a mission to protect archaeologists in Morocco. The film follows the tradition of earlier Legion classics like Beau Geste (1939) and Desert Legion (1953), depicting the harsh realities and complex moral choices faced by the infamous French Foreign Legion. What sets this film apart is its focus on the clash between military duty and archaeological preservation during France's colonial period, predating similar themes explored in Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981).

sections.content: The French Foreign Legion subgenre peaked in the 1930s-1950s with films like Under Two Flags (1936) and Ten Tall Men (1951). These movies typically romanticized Legion life while emphasizing themes of redemption, honor, and escape from the past. March or Die takes a grittier approach, reflecting the post-Vietnam era's more cynical view of military institutions and colonialism. Hackman's performance as the world-weary Foster echoes similar anti-hero military commanders like Lancaster in The Professionals (1966). SUBHEAD: Colonial Legacy and Military Drama

The film's examination of French colonialism in North Africa connects to later works like The Wind and the Lion (1975) and The Battle of Algiers (1966). Director Dick Richards crafts intense desert sequences that influenced later Legion-themed films like Legionnaire (1998) with Jean-Claude Van Damme. The archaeological subplot presages similar themes in The English Patient (1996), where military and scholarly pursuits collide against a backdrop of war.
